body_ar:
إن الخلاف من ضرورات التعايش، فقد جعل الله البشر متفاوتين في الخِلقة والخلق والعقل، وهذا التنوع والاختلاف ناتج عن اختلاف العقول، ومن تفاوتت عقولهم فبالإمكان أن تتفاوت اتجاهاتهم، وألا تتحد رؤاهم ومواقفهم، وكل ذلك واقع، وفقه الخلاف يرتكز على بيان خطر الاختلاف والتحذير منه، وبيان أنواعه، وآدابه، وعلاجه، وما يجوز من الخلاف وما لا يجوز.
الخلاف من ضرورات التعايش:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه، واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. موضوع هذا الدرس: (فقه الخلاف) والعناصر التي سنتعرض لها فيه هي: أولاً: التحذير من الفرقة والاختلاف. ثانيًا: أنوع الخلاف. ثالثًا: آداب المتخالفين. رابعًا: علاج الخلاف. إن الخلاف من ضرورات التعايش، فقد جعل الله البشر متفاوتين في الخِلقة والخلق والعقل، وميَّز بعضهم على بعض، وهذا التنوع الذي جعلهم الله عليه مقتضٍ لئلا يتفقوا في بعض المسائل، وعدم اتفاقهم فيه إثراء وفائدة للبشر، وفائدة لأهل الأرض ..
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Disagreement is one of the things that living together cannot do without. God made human beings differ in constitution, in disposition and in intellect, and this variety and this difference result from the difference of intellects; and those whose intellects differ may well differ in their inclinations, and their views and their positions may not be one. All of that is a fact. Understanding disagreement rightly rests on setting out the danger of disagreement and warning against it, on setting out its kinds, its proprieties and its remedy, and on what is permissible in the way of disagreement and what is not.

## Disagreement is one of the things living together cannot do without

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. The subject of this lesson is "Understanding Disagreement Rightly", and the elements we shall take up in it are:

First: the warning against splitting apart and against disagreement.
Second: the kinds of disagreement.
Third: the proprieties of those who differ with one another.
Fourth: the remedy for disagreement.

Disagreement is one of the things living together cannot do without. God made human beings differ in constitution, in disposition and in intellect, and gave some of them distinction over others; and this variety in which God has set them entails that they should not agree on certain questions. Their not agreeing on it is an enrichment and a benefit to human beings, and a benefit to the people of the earth ..

flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off after the four elements have been named and the first sentence of the first element given, with none of the four expounded — including what is permissible in the way of disagreement and what is not, which the synopsis promises. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/g-22.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson

present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the title of the first element, the opening of the synopsis and the Sheikh's own first sentence
options: one of the things that living together cannot do without
one of the necessities of coexistence
flags.note: A glossary homonym that must not be taken across. 'ضرورة' in legal theory is the technical threshold of necessity that permits the otherwise forbidden, and the glossary warns expressly that it is not general hardship. Nothing of that sense is in play here: the claim is descriptive, that people living together will inevitably differ. The third option would read as though disagreement were being licensed under the doctrine of necessity, which is not what the sentence says. The first has been chosen precisely because it cannot be mistaken for the technical term.

flags.context: the title, repeated in the synopsis and in the Sheikh's own announcement of the subject
flags.note: 'فقه' in the compound 'فقه X' is the developed and disciplined understanding of a subject rather than jurisprudence in the narrow sense, as in 'فقه الأولويات' and 'فقه الواقع'. 'The Jurisprudence of Disagreement' is the more literal rendering and is recorded, but it would suggest to an English reader a body of law about disagreement, which is not what the four announced elements describe. The choice should be settled corpus-wide rather than record by record, since the compound recurs.

flags.arabic: وما يجوز من الخلاف وما لا يجوز
flags.context: the closing words of the site's synopsis
options: what is permissible in the way of disagreement and what is not
which disagreements are allowed and which are not
what disagreement is licit and what is illicit
flags.note: A ruling word, and the single thing a reader of this record would most want. 'يجوز' is the verb of 'جائز' and the English gives 'permissible' per the fixed mapping. The served text never reaches it: the lesson stops after the first sentence of the first element, so the line between permissible and impermissible disagreement — which is the whole practical point of the subject — is promised by the synopsis and delivered nowhere. Anyone displaying this record must not let it appear to answer that question.

flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, style guide section 11. 'أنواع' is served as 'أنوع'; the same word is spelled correctly in the synopsis of this record. Preserved in body_ar and not repaired.

flags.context: the Sheikh's first sentence, and the synopsis
options: differ in constitution, in disposition and in intellect
differ in physical make-up, in character and in mind
flags.note: 'الخِلقة' and 'الخُلق' are distinguished in the source by a single vowel, which the source marks on the first — bodily constitution as against moral disposition. The pun is unrenderable and the English keeps the distinction rather than the sound. Note that the source vocalises 'الخِلقة' here, one of very few vocalisations anywhere in this slice, which suggests the transcriber saw the same difficulty.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The subject overlaps closely with record 725 of this run and record 707 of the creed run, and the three should be read together once the full texts are in. This record is the most valuable of the three, because its first sentence states a positive thesis — that difference among people is inevitable and is a benefit — which the other two do not.
The English sets the four elements as a list where the source runs them on with ordinals, which is how the source itself presents them. No word has been added.
The source ends with two dots rather than three; reproduced as served.
